extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and practitioners working on headline generation, clickbait detection, and reinforcement learning
extracted.subtask_description: Generate abstractive headlines that maximize reader attention ('sensational' or clickbait) using reinforcement learning, while preserving naturalness by balancing RL rewards with likelihood-based training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sensational headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensational headlines are headlines that capture people's attention and generate reader interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the working definition used to motivate the task and to design the sensationalism scorer and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensationalism training proxy (many-comments clickbait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Train a sensationalism scorer by classifying online headlines with many comments ("clickbait") against a baseline of headlines generated from a summarization model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses number of comments on online headlines as a proxy label for sensationalism/clickbait; the scorer is trained to distinguish high-comment ('clickbait') headlines from summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sensationalism score as RL reward
rubrics_metrics.description: The score from the sensationalism scorer is used as the reward for a reinforcement learner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sensationalism scorer's output becomes the optimization target for the headline generation policy; note that this reward can be noisy and must be handled carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness / fluency constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximizing the noisy sensationalism reward will generate unnatural phrases instead of sensational headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoiding degenerate/ungrammatical outputs is an explicit quality criterion: models should produce sensational headlines that remain natural and well-formed; thus optimization must account for language quality, not only reward score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auto-tuned Reinforcement Learning (ARL) — balance between RL and MLE
rubrics_metrics.description: Auto-tuned Reinforcement Learning (ARL) is a novel loss function proposed to dynamically balance reinforcement learning (RL) with maximum likelihood estimation (MLE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARL is presented as the mechanism to effectively leverage a noisy sensationalism reward by trading off reward maximization and likelihood-based fluency preservation; the dynamic balancing is a methodological requirement to meet both sensationalism and naturalness criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation of sensationalness
rubrics_metrics.description: Human evaluation is used to judge whether generated headlines are sensational; the paper reports that 60.8% of samples generated by the model are sensational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use human judgments as a primary evaluation metric for sensational quality (rather than only automatic scorers); report proportions/percentages judged sensational and statistical comparisons versus baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison against baselines (e.g., Pointer-Gen and other RL models)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate generated headlines relative to existing baselines: Pointer-Gen summarization baseline and other RL models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate improvement in sensationalness (and presumably in naturalness/overall quality) by comparing quantitatively (human evaluation percentages) and/or via automatic metrics against established baselines.
